question: With the fanout stage enabled and the full pipeline after it, does krt-qfn-escape (straight escape stubs on QFN, QFP, SOIC and SOP parts at a pitch of at most 0.65 mm, widened past the pin field or ending in a plane via, then Freerouting's fanout on the other parts) leave fewer unrouted connections than Freerouting's fanout, without new clearance violations, vias in pads or more copper under its class width?
hypothesis: none registered: the X10 checklist names no expected direction; the measurement decides whether the stage stays selectable

freerouting-fanout.engine: freerouting-rs at the commit that lands X10, after P04's default-tree decision, in-process through freerouting-krt's harness (the CLI does not call freerouting_krt::register before C07)
freerouting-fanout.command: X10_DSN={DSN} X10_ARMS=freerouting-fanout X10_SES_DIR={SES_DIR} cargo test --release -p freerouting-krt --test qfn_escape escape_arms_on_a_set -- --ignored --exact --nocapture

krt-qfn-escape.command: X10_DSN={DSN} X10_ARMS=krt-qfn-escape X10_SES_DIR={SES_DIR} cargo test --release -p freerouting-krt --test qfn_escape escape_arms_on_a_set -- --ignored --exact --nocapture

boards.eligibility_rule: a board with at least one part freerouting_krt::fanout::frame::analyze qualifies (qualifying_parts_on_a_set on the input board); the five canary-pwr variants count as one board in the pass rule (their results move by about 10 unrouted with small input changes, as in Q02.6) and are reported each

eligibility: every board of the set; a board where both arms leave the same number unrouted is neutral, printed; a board not graded (a crash, a timeout, exit 2 of a grader) fails that board for the arm that was not graded and is never a pass

grading.canary-pwr: the SES of each arm goes to the CANary layout session (canary-23) as in X01; until its grade exists canary-pwr counts as not graded for both arms (no win for either); Rust's DRC numbers are printed beside it
grading.coldfire: tools/kicad-oracle/grade.sh on the KiCad demo kit-dev-coldfire-xilinx_5213 prepared as X01 prepared it, with the arm's command as ENGINE_COMMAND: the board's original rules, copper severities forced to error, the input board's DRC subtracted; drc_real, kicad_unconnected and via_in_pad from the grader. If the grader cannot run, Rust's DRC grades it and the amendment says so
grading.others: no .kicad_pcb in the repository: graded by Rust's DRC inside the harness (drc_new: all_clearance_violations of the routed board with an item the run created) and its via-in-pad test

metrics.name: drc_real
metrics.source: the KiCad grader where it runs; drc_new from Rust's DRC otherwise

metrics.name: unrouted
metrics.source: kicad_unconnected on KiCad-graded boards; the routed board's airlines (DesignRulesChecker::all_airlines) otherwise

metrics.name: under_width_mm
metrics.source: Q02.1: freerouting::quality::neckdown::width_report::report(routed).under_total() in mm (copper under its net's class width, taper steps included)

keep_rule: krt-qfn-escape stays a selectable fanout stage (off by default) only if unrouted improves on N-1 of the graded boards and regresses on none, with via_in_pad and drc_real 0 for it on every board and under_width_mm no higher than Freerouting's fanout on any board (a higher value is a regression on that board). Otherwise the stage registration is removed (the frame module may stay for X12) and the numbers stay in X10.4's done note. Either way it is never a default from this run.

decision_table.keep: krt-qfn-escape stays registered; docs/DIVERGENCES.md gets its line (a selectable stage Java does not have)
decision_table.reject: the registration goes; X10.4 records the numbers

stop_rule: one run per board and arm; no re-run except for a crash or a not-graded board, which is re-run once and reported
timing: the registered run waits for P04's default-tree decision (P00 README 'Order', Q00 README 'Order and critical path'); X10.4's partial note gives a pre-P04 dry run at the landing tree, labelled as such, not this registration's result

amendments.reason: Before the first engine run of the registered run (after P04's decision, c23d8c0: the default tree stays Java's). (1) The grading clause routes kit-dev-coldfire through tools/kicad-oracle/grade.sh on the KiCad demo prepared as X01 prepared it, so the input the arms route is the DSN grade.sh exports from that prepared board, not the fixture fixtures/Issue690-kit-dev-coldfire-xilinx_5213.dsn: the row is renamed kit-dev-coldfire-xilinx_5213 and registered with the prepared board's sha256 (X01's and X06's registration; target/orchestrator/x01/boards/kit-dev-coldfire-xilinx_5213/prepared). The exported DSN embeds its work path in its first line; its body hashes to 4758a3f1b85f0969f4adbc47d0bf0f3c26448677fbe7023f1e32a27068c9a6d0. canary-pwr-9511d9a is graded on WSL KiCad 10.0.7 by canary-23's tools (canary HEAD 1a7df77b: ses_import.py onto the board at sha256 15aa06a3 = 9511d9a, via_in_pad.py, inner_tracks.py) with tools/krt-h2h/grade_routed.sh for drc_real and unconnected items (input DRC subtracted); the canary-23 session is not involved. The four variants come from older board states that the board at 9511d9a cannot import, so they are graded by Rust's DRC inside the harness, as the other fixtures. (2) The harness starts from an empty settings patch (default_profile in the crate's test file), not TestingProfile::default(), whose copper-to-edge clearance 0 (java_fixture_test) biased the pre-P04 dry run. Each route runs under a 45 min timeout; a timed-out arm is not graded, which the eligibility rule already makes a failed board for that arm.
